meta.title: SuCSS — a classless CSS framework for plain HTML
meta.description: A classless CSS framework. Write plain semantic HTML — no class names, no custom attributes — and get liquid-glass surfaces, dark mode and accessibility with it.
hero.lead: SuCSS is a classless CSS framework. Write plain HTML — <header>, <table>, <button> — and liquid-glass surfaces, dark mode and accessibility come with it. No class names, no custom attributes, no build step.
hero.claim: This page is the demo. It carries no class attribute anywhere. Paste the line below into your <head> and your own HTML looks like this.
hero.name: Su (素) is Japanese for plain, or unadorned.
features.heading: Features
features.classless.title: No class names
features.classless.body: Styling comes from the elements themselves. There is no naming convention to agree on and no utility classes to memorise.
features.dark.title: Dark mode included
features.dark.body: Follows prefers-color-scheme, and data-theme pins it either way.
features.a11y.title: Accessible by default
features.a11y.body: WCAG AA/AAA contrast, visible :focus-visible rings, adequate touch targets. It honours prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-reduced-transparency too.
features.glass.title: Liquid glass
features.glass.body: Surfaces behave like a lens rather than a frosted sheet: the backdrop stays legible through them, colour blooms out of them, and every edge carries a rim of light.
features.small.title: One file, no dependencies
features.small.body: A single stylesheet, 4.7 KB minified and gzipped. No JavaScript, no build step.
features.tokens.title: Tuned with variables
features.tokens.body: Every colour, radius and rhythm is a custom property. Change --hue and the whole page moves — try it in the customizer.
install.heading: Install
install.lead: For the CDN, paste the line above into your <head>. With a bundler, install it from npm.
install.table.caption: What ships
install.support: Supported browsers are Chrome/Edge 111+, Safari 16.4+ and Firefox 128+. Without backdrop-filter, surfaces fall back to solid fills.
elements.heading: Elements
elements.lead: Everything below is plain HTML with no class attribute. Open the page source and compare.
elements.text.heading: Text
elements.text.body: Paragraphs are set from --line-height and --max-width. Strong, emphasis, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, Ctrl + C, CSS, x, output, a defined term, subscript, superscript and a link all come styled.
elements.quote.body: The hours you would spend designing class names go into designing the semantics instead.
elements.quote.cite: — on going back to plain HTML
elements.aside.heading: Aside
elements.aside.body: <aside> reads as a note set apart from the body text.
elements.lists.heading: Lists
elements.lists.ul2c: Switching to numbers changes nothing else
elements.lists.ul3: The element is the unit of style
elements.lists.dd1: Styling a page through element selectors alone, with no class attributes.
elements.lists.dd2: A surface that lets the backdrop through, blooms its colour, and carries light on its edges.
elements.table.heading: Tables
elements.table.caption: The main custom properties and their defaults
tokens.hue: The accent colour and the background mesh
tokens.blur: How far the glass blurs its backdrop
elements.table.foot: All of them can be overridden in :root.
elements.form.heading: Forms
elements.form.name: Name
elements.buttons.heading: Buttons and states
elements.buttons.toolbarNote: A toolbar asks Tab to enter it once and the arrow keys to move inside. SuCSS draws the bar; that keyboard behaviour is yours to write. Use role="group" when you cannot.
elements.buttons.details: Regions that open and close are elements too.
elements.dialog.heading: Dialog
elements.dialog.body: <dialog> and the backdrop behind it are both styled.
elements.media.heading: Code and media
elements.media.body: Code blocks scroll sideways rather than pushing the page. <figure> with a <figcaption> is handled too.
elements.media.caption: The brand assets live in assets/brand/.
customizing.heading: Customizing
customizing.lead: Colours, radii, spacing and type are all custom properties. A few lines in :root move the whole page — or open the customizer and drag the controls until it looks right.
customizing.pin.heading: Pinning a theme
customizing.pin.body: By default the theme follows the operating system. data-theme on <html> pins it — which is all the buttons at the top of this page do.
customizer.meta.title: Customize SuCSS
customizer.meta.description: Move the controls and this page restyles itself. Copy the resulting :root block into your own stylesheet.
customizer.heading: Customize
customizer.tagline: Every value below is a CSS custom property.
customizer.lead: Move a control and this page changes with it — it is styled by the same stylesheet you are tuning, so what you see is what your own pages will look like. Nothing here is a setting inside SuCSS: it is plain CSS you paste into :root.
customizer.storage: Your choices are kept in this browser and follow you to the rest of the site. Reset puts everything back.
customizer.outputLead: Only the properties you changed are listed. Paste them after the stylesheet link and they win on specificity alone.
customizer.outputEmpty: /* Nothing changed yet — move a control above. */
customizer.previewLead: The whole page is the preview, but these are the pieces the accent colour reaches first.
customizer.fieldPlaceholder: Focus me to see the ring
customizer.quote: Type is the loudest thing on a page. Set it first, then the colour.
